html:
Remark. Neutron: NF construction, mass, transition, and charge

The neutron definition establishes the \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d},\mathfrak{d}) baryon. We derive its normal form, mass, \beta-decay transition, and Coulomb charge.

Step 1: Borromean braid NF. As in the proton construction, we find \mathrm{net}(\mathcal{B}_3) = +1.000, establishing intrinsic Hopf link content without an independent \mathcal{L}_H factor.

Step 2: Typed crossings + Hopf gluon stabilisation. The two down quarks induce stronger -h_{\mathrm{A}} shifts than the single down quark of the proton. The crossing pairs appear in Table: Neutron crossing pairs.

(Partly withdrawn — see below. Two independent corrections, four days apart.)

The bare 9-crossing element \mathcal{B}_3 \times \Delta_3(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) remains LP unstable. The \sigma_0 channel violates Frobenius positivity following the second quark crossing. A single Hopf link L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 is what the construction applies.

The integer LP dual selects L_- as the minimum-action stabiliser, for a total of 11 crossings (6 from \mathcal{B}_3, 3 from quarks, 2 from gluons) — qou-vtlj, which rebuilt the block's own recipe and found the stated \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) = +0.7976 is the eleven-crossing value. The earlier "L_+ \to L_-, 4 gluon crossings, 13 total" was wrong on its own terms, independently of anything below.

The \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing creates a deeper instability than the proton's (\mathrm{tr}_M = -0.132 versus -0.006), a difference in depth rather than in the number of gluon crossings required.

The remaining depth claim does not survive either (qou-jqjx). Those two figures come from computations/_deprecated/integer-lp-gluon.py, which computes the Markov trace on convention C with \mathrm{tr}_M(e^-) = z^3 — a weight retired on 2026-05-19 in favour of the Markov-recursion value h z^2 + z. Reproduced on the retired convention the numbers come out at -0.132224 and -0.005936, matching what was published. On the live convention the same elements are +0.408 and +0.544, and the \sigma_0 channel is positive at every step of the typed build. There is no instability, deeper or otherwise, and so no depth difference to carry a mass split.

Note the sequence, because it is the point: correcting the crossing count removed the 4-versus-2 asymmetry and moved the surviving claim onto the two numbers that are themselves convention artefacts. Both corrections are needed; neither alone finishes the paragraph.

What replaces it is open. Nothing is offered here — the derivation needs re-deriving rather than patching, and the gluon ledger carries the full measurement.

What survives unchanged is the scope of the enumeration: every non-trivial braid word inside the crossing cap, the trefoil word e^- included, admissible and simply losing the minimisation.

Step 3: Neutron NF (with Hopf gluon). At q_0 \approx 1.1100:

See Table.

  \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) = +0.7976

Relative to the proton (\mathrm{net} = +1.0065), the additional down quark demands a larger L_+ compensation (-0.2206 versus -0.1114). After Hopf gluon stabilisation, the trefoil channel e^- \approx +1.0 dominates both nucleons.

Transition: proton \to neutron. The normal-form difference yields the dimensionless \beta-decay transition (energy scale):

  \Delta\mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n} - \mathfrak{p})
  = 0.7976 - 1.0065 = -0.2089

The uniform energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / |\Delta\mathrm{net}| \approx 4.155 MeV converts these coefficient differences directly to MeV (formation chain).

Mass.

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} =
  2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}}(q) + \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}}(q)

At the CODATA value q_0, the base mass is \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}}(q_0) \approx 939.565\;\text{MeV} MeV, derived strictly from the substrate parameter (local substrate). The resulting proton--neutron mass splitting is exactly:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} =
  \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}}(q) - \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}}(q)
  \approx 1.293 \text{ MeV}

This splitting arises from the Skein resolution asymmetry between the \mathfrak{u}\text{-}\mathfrak{u} and \mathfrak{d}\text{-}\mathfrak{d} crossing pairs within the rigid \mathcal{B}_3 structure.

Coulomb charge.

  Q(\mathfrak{n}) =
  1 \cdot (+\tfrac{2}{3}) + 2 \cdot (-\tfrac{1}{3}) = 0.

The sum vanishes, and the arithmetic is the Standard Model's. What it is not is a consequence of the crossing-orientation mechanism. This block previously read that the single positive-orientation unknot \mathfrak{u} cancels two negative-orientation unknots \mathfrak{d}; one object cannot cancel two of equal magnitude. The cancellation above works only because |Q_{\mathfrak{u}}| = 2|Q_{\mathfrak{d}}|, and orientation reversal is a mirror, so it forces the two magnitudes to be equal (down quark). Writing Q(\mathfrak{u}) = a and hence Q(\mathfrak{d}) = -a, the neutron carries a - 2a = -a and the proton 2a - a = +a: the mechanism makes the neutron the proton's exact opposite, and a neutral neutron forces every quark charge to vanish (QOU.Braiding.mirror_odd_neutral_neutron_forces_zero, sorry-free). The quark charges are therefore an adopted input here, not a derived one. The inter-neutron Hopf crossings acquire the q^{-1} coefficient associated with negative crossings.
